Courtney Lorey is an environmental specialist with a foundation in marine science and ocean policy. Building on more than five years of experience in ocean conservation, she is currently pursuing a Master of Environmental Data Science to explore how large-scale ocean datasets can inform conservation policy and management decisions.

Prior to joining the Bren School, Courtney worked on the National Geographic Pristine Seas team, where she supported more than fifteen country projects focused on establishing new marine protected areas. Through policy, communications, and strategic planning, her work contributed to the protection of more than 260,000 square kilometers of ocean — an area roughly equivalent to the size of New Zealand. 

Previously, Courtney worked as a policy intern at Oceana, a fisheries observer for the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration, and a research assistant at the Virginia Institute of Marine Science. She holds a B.S. in Biology with a minor in Marine Science from the College of William & Mary.
